problem_motivation.content: Producing refractory metal high entropy alloys using conventional metallurgical methods is difficult.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: producing refractory metal high entropy alloys by conventional metallurgical methods remains challenging

problem_motivation.content: Only a small fraction of possible refractory metal high entropy alloy compositions are investigated due to challenging manufacturing conditions.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Despite first investigations, currently only a small fracture of the possible compositions of refractory metal high entropy alloys is investigated.

prior_approach.content: Cantor et al. independently reported the formation of multi-component alloys in 2004.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The formation of such multi component alloys was reported independently by Cantor et al. [ [1] ] and the research group around J.-W. Yeh in 2004

prior_approach.content: Senkov et al. reported results on specific refractory metal high entropy alloys in 2010 and 2011.
prior_approach.evidence_span: First results on the alloys WMoTaNb and WMoTaNbV were reported by Senkov et al., in 2010 [ [18] ] and 2011 [ [19] ], respectively.

prior_approach.content: The alloy W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 was previously developed and investigated by Senkov et al.
prior_approach.evidence_span: W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 is one of the first refractory metal high entropy alloys developed by Senkov et al. [ [18] ]

prior_approach.content: Previous work reported undissolved Mo particles in Ti-alloys produced by in-situ alloy formation and PBF-LB/M.
prior_approach.evidence_span: E.g., Yadroitsev et al. [ [42] ] report undissolved Mo particles in Ti-alloys produced by in-situ alloy formation and PBF-LB/M

prior_approach.content: Literature indicates hot cracking is a common defect in Al wrought alloys during PBF-LB/M.
prior_approach.evidence_span: One mechanism, the so called hot cracking, which is related to the solidification of the alloy, is often reported for PBF-LB/M of e.g., Al wrought alloys like the EN AW 6xxx [ [44] ] or EN AW 2xxx [ [45] ] series.

prior_approach.content: Prior literature establishes the temperature gradient mechanism model for internal stress formation during PBF-LB/M.
prior_approach.evidence_span: According to the temperature gradient mechanism model that describes the formation of internal stress during PBF-LB/M [ [47] , [48] ]

prior_limitation.content: Refractory metal high entropy alloys are far less investigated compared to 3d transition metal alloys.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: In contrast to that, refractory metal high entropy alloys are by far less investigated [ [7] ].

prior_limitation.content: Refractory metal high entropy alloy manufacturing is challenging due to high melting temperatures, wide melting point ranges, and segregation tendencies.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Due to the high melting temperatures, the wide range of melting points of refractory metals (e.g., Vanadium at 1910 °C [ [26] ] vs. Tungsten at 3422 °C [ [26] ]), and the tendency to segregate during solidification, manufacturing of refractory metal high entropy alloys is challenging.

prior_limitation.content: Existing Directed Energy Deposition (DED) methods limit geometries and require additional re-melting steps.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: In contrast to conventional DED, Dobbelstein et al. are not welding continuous weld seams but stack spot welds onto each other to form cylindrical samples, which limits the geometries that can be manufactured. Also, a re-melting step without powder flow is necessary for homogenization of the element distribution and to avoid unmolten particles.

prior_limitation.content: Prior PBF-LB/M research on refractory metal high entropy alloys lacked detailed microstructural and homogeneity analysis.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, only small-scale SEM-images and basic corrosion resistance measurements are shown and further research is necessary to understand the effect of the PBF-LB/M processing conditions on the material properties and the homogeneity of the element distribution after in-situ alloy formation.

prior_limitation.content: Due to the youth of the field and vast number of combinations, most alloy combinations have only single publications with limited information.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Since the concept of refractory metal high entropy alloys is comparably young, and the number of possible alloy combinations is vast, there are only single publications on most of the different alloy combinations, thus providing only limited information per alloy.

prior_limitation.content: Prior work noted a parameter dependence of remaining high melting particles but did not fully explain the specific interdependencies in the current alloy context until now.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, they also reported a parameter dependence of the amount of remaining high melting particles. These interdependencies between the PBF-LB/M process parameters and the amount of undissolved high melting particles at in-situ alloy formation are discussed extensively in one of our previous publications [ [32] ].

prior_limitation.content: Existing understanding of the WMoTaNb alloy notes very limited ductility and fracture toughness at room temperature, which the current paper attributes to grain boundary embrittlement.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: According to the results of Zou et al. [ [46] ] and Senkov et al. [ [19] ] the alloy WMoTaNb possesses only a very limited degree of ductility and fracture toughness at room temperature.

rejected_alternative.content: Spherical V-powder was not used because it could not be obtained.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Spherical V-powder could unfortunately not be obtained. Hence, milled V-powder from NMD New Materials Development GmbH (Heemsen, Germany) was used.

causal_claim.content: The specific parameter set PBF-LB/M B (lower scan speed, higher energy density) facilitates the dissolution of high melting W particles, leading to fewer undissolved particles.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This facilitates the dissolution of the high melting W particles, thus leading to less undissolved particles as shown in Figure 2 .

mechanism_principle.content: The smaller grain size in the current study is caused by the high cooling rates inherent to the PBF-LB/M process.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is more than a factor of four smaller than the 80 µm reported by Senkov et al. for vacuum arc molten samples. The smaller grain size can be attributed to the high cooling rates in the range of 10 6 K/s during the PBF-LB/M process [ [50] ].

mechanism_principle.content: The coarser structures at interlayer boundaries are caused by smaller temperature gradients in the liquid and smaller growth rates at outer contours compared to inner regions.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: According to [ [51] ] temperature gradients in the liquid and growth rates are smaller at the outer contours of the meltpool compared to the inner regions, explaining the coarser structures

mechanism_principle.content: Solidification mode and structure size are determined by the ratio of growth rate (R) to temperature gradient (G), where specific combinations favor columnar or cellular structures.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: According to the literature [ [52] , [53] ] the solidification mode and also the structure size is determined by R and G. While higher growth rates R and lower temperature gradients G in the liquid favor a columnar dendritic solidification, lower growth rates R and higher temperature gradients in the liquid G favor cellular solidification.

hypothesis_statement.content: The feasibility of using laser powder bed fusion with in-situ alloy formation to produce the specific refractory metal high entropy alloy will be demonstrated.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: the feasibility of laser-based additive manufacturing of the refractory metal high entropy alloy W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 by laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) is investigated

hypothesis_statement.content: The study proposes to explore the processing of the specific refractory metal high entropy alloy via PBF-LB/M and analyze parameter influences.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In this context, the aim of the present work is to explore processing of the refectory metal high entropy alloy W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 by PBF-LB/M and to examine the influence of the process parameters on the resulting microstructural properties.

hypothesis_statement.content: The low laser power/low scan speed parameter set was chosen with the expectation that it would support the dissolution of W in the meltpool.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The low laser power/low scan speed parameter set PBF-LB/M B was furthermore derived from previous work on in-situ alloy formation strategies with high melting particles and is assumed to support dissolution of W in the meltpool [ [32] ].

evidence_result.content: Samples achieved a relative density of 99.8% under favorable process parameters.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The relative density of the samples with a dimension of 6 × 6 × 6 mm 3 reaches, in dependence of the PBF-LB/M parameter set, 99.8%

evidence_result.content: Measurements confirm the material consists of a single body-centered cubic (bcc) phase.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) measurements confirm the presence of a single bcc-phase

evidence_result.content: Microstructural analysis revealed a dendritic and/or cellular structure that is partially controllable via process parameters.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images show a dendritic and/or cellular microstructure that can, to some extent, be controlled by the PBF-LB/M parameters

evidence_result.content: The microhardness of the PBF-LB/M A sample is measured at 561 ± 17 HV0.1.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The microhardness of the PBF-LB/M A sample with the coarser structure is 561 ± 17 HV0.1 (n = 9)

evidence_result.content: The microhardness of the PBF-LB/M B sample is measured at 614 ± 21 HV0.1.
evidence_result.evidence_span: while the microhardness of the PBF-LB/M B sample is 614 ± 21 HV0.1 (n = 9).

constraint.content: The powder mixture must have sufficient flowability to be recoated to thin layers (20-100 µm) to enable PBF-LB/M.
constraint.evidence_span: To facilitate PBF-LB/M in the first place, it is mandatory that the powder mixture has sufficient flowability and can be recoated to thin layers [ [38] , [39] ], typically ranging between 20 µm and 100 µm for PBF-LB/M.

constraint.content: The oxygen content of the process gas must be kept below 25 ppm to minimize oxygen intake.
constraint.evidence_span: The oxygen content of the process gas was constantly kept below 25 ppm during PBF-LB/M processing to keep oxygen intake low.
